reasoning: I independently read the full stem, both parts and every existing marking step. Translating y=ln x two units left and ln4 up gives f(x)=ln(4x+8), x>-2. Its intercepts are (-7/4,0) and (0,ln8), so the unique finite region bounded by the curve and both axes lies in quadrant II. For 0<=y<=ln8 the curve is x=e^y/4-2<=0; the physical disk radius is 2-e^y/4. Thus V=pi integral_0^ln8 (2-e^y/4)^2 dy = pi[e^(2y)/32-e^y+4y]_0^ln8 = pi(4ln8-161/32). The existing squared negative x-expression gives the same integral. The original final answer is also correct because its giant integer is exactly 2^384. Replacing that final A1 text with the readable equivalent changes presentation only, with no change to the problem, marking allocation or mathematical answer.
